P2pKit embedded JmDNS modifications

Upstream: org.jmdns:jmdns:3.6.3, tag v3.6.3,
commit 93b326381940f3fcd250d770a14a36de4c2dfcda.
Private component revision: 3.6.3-p2pkit.410.8.

Mechanical integration relocates the complete javax.jmdns production package
into dev.p2pkit.transport.lan.internal.jmdns. Java source uses LF line endings,
no trailing spaces or tabs, and exactly one final newline. Added modification
notices do not replace the original license headers or author attributions.
Version and command-line diagnostic resource lookups use the private
version.properties path instead of a root resource or upstream Maven descriptor.
LICENSE is preserved byte-for-byte. NOTICE.txt keeps the upstream substantive
text and attributions; only three trailing spaces were removed (775 original
bytes, 772 distributed bytes). PROVENANCE.json records the original NOTICE
digest separately from the normalized distributed resource.

patches/410-lifecycle.patch records the separate native lifecycle correction
against the mechanically relocated, normalized source baseline. Its bytes and
digest are unchanged by subsequent fixes.

patches/415-opt-rcode.patch corrects extended response-code extraction from the
whole OPT TTL for the existing wrong-version diagnostic. It does not change
the separate receive-header acceptance gate or the lifecycle correction.

patches/416-reverse-domain.patch recognizes reverse DNS namespaces only at
terminal DNS-name boundaries, not as substrings in ordinary service instances.
This preserves the DNS-SD event type for accepted legacy names containing
in-addr.arpa or ip6.arpa. The lifecycle and OPT diagnostic patches are unchanged.

patches/414-service-port.patch includes the service port in resolved-event
deduplication so a port-only update reaches the listener. Unchanged records
remain deduplicated; the lifecycle, OPT and reverse-domain patches are unchanged.

patches/417-response-continuation.patch preserves the requester destination and
transaction ID on every overflow continuation. Existing flags, payload capacity,
TC handling, record ordering and send failures remain unchanged. A protected
send forwarding method isolates the side effect for socket-free serialization
regressions; scheduled production tasks retain their original sender.

patches/418-teardown-budget.patch gives host cancellation one monotonic 5000ms
allowance shared by its services, recovery and terminal close. Recovery observes
terminal ownership between bounded cancellation waits and hands off without
losing still-owned resources. A failed send cannot multiply protocol waits per
service before disposal. The separate resource-drain budget, successful native
TTL-zero sends, actual resource ownership/disposal proof and interruption rules
remain required. Public service-unregister semantics and all SDK deadlines are
unchanged. Socket-free arithmetic checks are not real-resource qualification.

patches/503-cache-bounds.patch bounds the pre-admission DNS cache to 4096
records and an 8 MiB deterministic retained-byte charge, including variable
names, derived fields, TXT and fixed record/index overhead. This charge is not
an exact JVM heap-size measurement. Capacity eviction prefers expired records,
then oldest insertions; it notifies existing listeners outside cache/lifecycle
locks. Shared RRsets, exact-value TTL refresh, cache-flush grace and TTL-zero
goodbyes remain supported. Oversized replacements cannot flush a usable value.
The pressure warning is emitted at most once per handle, outside mutation locks.

Remote meta PTRs now obey the same cache/TTL budget as ordinary PTRs. Remote
types and subtypes are derived from live cached PTRs rather than permanently
registered: each has at most 4096 remote entries, backed by the record/byte
budget. A type survives while any cached owner still advertises it. Locally
registered or actively requested types are separately owned and survive remote
expiry/eviction. Type-listener deduplication history is limited to 8192 names
and an 8 MiB name/entry charge; forgotten types can be announced again. Successful
close clears cache/type bookkeeping only after existing disposal proof succeeds.
A package-private socket-free constructor supports deterministic original
parser/record/cache tests; production constructors always start networking.
This is bounded retention, not authenticated admission, fairness against Sybils,
physical discovery/soak evidence or native lifecycle qualification. Earlier
upstream and patch bytes are unchanged.

patches/516-txt-readiness.patch requires received or explicitly supplied TXT
before declaring service resolution complete. The wire-format getTextBytes()
fallback is still an empty TXT, but no longer invents resolution evidence for
SRV/address-only cache replay. This prevents a delayed pre-TXT callback from
withdrawing a newer complete peer admission, including across distinct resolver
infos. Actual empty TXT remains a complete DNS-SD record and still reaches
application metadata validation; unchanged complete info remains deduplicated.
Socket-free parser/cache/clone/executor and admission/relay regressions are not
multicast, macOS consumer or native lifecycle qualification. Earlier upstream
and patch bytes are unchanged.

PROVENANCE.json schema 2 preserves lifecyclePatch and lists subsequent patches
in followupPatches application order. All are zero-context unified patches:
from this vendor directory, apply the lifecycle patch first, then each followup
with git apply --unidiff-zero --whitespace=error-all. Verify the declared
relocated-baseline hashes before applying patches and the final source hashes
after the complete sequence. The manifest separately identifies original,
relocated-baseline and final source bytes and every patch digest. Patch replay
is a source-byte check, not build, runtime or release qualification.

Neither the private package nor its Java-public types are supported P2pKit API.
The upstream Maven identity is provenance, not a claim that these modified bytes
are the original upstream artifact or an independently published fork.
